concerns: The headline authority-bias contagion result (ΓA = 11.45) is explicitly non-replicable: all 15 controlled multi-seed runs yield ΓA = 0.00, so the abstract's authority-bias claim is not supported by reproducible evidence.

The only reproducible positive result (length bias, ΓA = 13.18) is confined to a single older model generation; newer same-family and cross-family models show complete immunity (ΓA = 0.00), undermining the claimed generality of Memory Contagion.

The evaluation is based on a very small synthetic task set (20 open-ended QA tasks, 12 train + 6 eval) with rejection-sampling bias injection that the authors acknowledge may co-select unmeasured quality features, leaving the core effect potentially confounded.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: Given that the phenomenon completely fails to replicate for authority bias under controlled conditions and does not manifest in newer or different model families for length bias, evidence for Memory Contagion as a general property of LLM agent memory architectures remains weak and uncertain.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The headline authority-bias contagion result (ΓA = 11.45) is explicitly non-replicable: all 15 controlled multi-seed runs yield ΓA = 0.00, so the abstract's authority-bias claim is not supported by reproducible evidence.

The only reproducible positive result (length bias, ΓA = 13.18) is confined to a single older model generation; newer same-family and cross-family models show complete immunity (ΓA = 0.00), undermining the claimed generality of Memory Contagion.

The evaluation is based on a very small synthetic task set (20 open-ended QA tasks, 12 train + 6 eval) with rejection-sampling bias injection that the authors acknowledge may co-select unmeasured quality features, leaving the core effect potentially confounded.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The paper studies an empirical phenomenon of bias propagation using explicit behavioral metric comparisons rather than optimizing a system against an automated judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Wasserstein distance (W1) between distributions of evaluator scores (response length and authority marker counts) on target agent responses.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rejection sampling during bias injection selects source agent responses maximizing the biased evaluator score (length or authority markers).

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: While the authors honestly document negative multi-seed replications and model immunity in the text and appendices, the title and abstract still introduce Memory Contagion and authority bias numbers (ΓA = 11.45) derived from non-replicable exploratory runs, resulting in tension with the evidence that authority bias does not replicate and length bias does not generalize beyond an older model generation.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical findings show substantial fragility: authority bias completely fails to propagate across all 15 controlled multi-seed experiments (yielding Γ = 0.00), leaving the preliminary positive authority numbers non-replicable. Furthermore, length bias contagion vanishes entirely (Γ = 0.00) in newer/stronger models (DeepSeek V4-Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6), isolating the observed phenomenon to an older model and a single bias type on a small synthetic task set.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Wasserstein distance (W1) between distributions of evaluator scores (response length and authority marker counts) on target agent responses.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rejection sampling during bias injection selects source agent responses maximizing the biased evaluator score (length or authority markers).

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose that authority bias failed to propagate in all 15 controlled runs, that newer models show zero contagion, and that additive separability and rejection-sampling bias injection may introduce confounds.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology formalizes bias propagation by comparing target agent behavior retrieving from biased vs. clean memory stores across consolidation conditions. However, the evaluation relies on a very small set of open-ended QA tasks (20 tasks, 12 train and 6 eval), and synthetic rejection sampling whose validity is admitted to risk co-selecting unmeasured quality features.
primary.quality_rationale: Given that the phenomenon completely fails to replicate for authority bias under controlled conditions and does not manifest in newer or different model families for length bias, evidence for Memory Contagion as a general property of LLM agent memory architectures remains weak and uncertain.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper investigates 'Memory Contagion'—the propagation of evaluator bias across episodes via external agent memory stores—formalizing a distributional metric (Wasserstein distance of behavioral scores) and evaluating it across length and authority biases under oracle and LLM consolidation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: Given that the phenomenon completely fails to replicate for authority bias under controlled conditions and does not manifest in newer or different model families for length bias, evidence for Memory Contagion as a general property of LLM agent memory architectures remains weak and uncertain.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly disclose that authority bias failed to propagate in all 15 controlled runs, that newer models show zero contagion, and that additive separability and rejection-sampling bias injection may introduce confounds.
